sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Diwani Rights**: Granted by Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, giving the EIC the right to collect land revenue in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. 
• **Nizamat Rights**: Retained by the Nawab, covering criminal justice, police, and law and order. 
• **Separation of Power and Responsibility**: The EIC held the 'power' (money) without 'responsibility' (administration), while the Nawab held the 'responsibility' without the 'power' (funds). 
• **Key Metric**: The system led to the 'Drain of Wealth' as revenue was used to purchase Indian goods for export, effectively stripping the province of capital.

items.title: Major Consequences
items.content:
• **Economic Ruin**: Excessive taxation led to the impoverishment of the peasantry. 
• **Administrative Collapse**: The 1770 Bengal Famine killed 1/3rd of the population due to neglect of irrigation and relief.

items.title: Termination
items.content:
• **Warren Hastings**: Abolished the Dual System in 1772, bringing the Company under direct administrative control. 
• **Centralization**: Shifted the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-N-A' (Diwani-Nawab-Abolished). 
• **Decoded Meaning**: Diwani (EIC), Nizamat (Nawab), Abolished (by Warren Hastings in 1772).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Dual System' (1765-1772) with 'Diarchy' (1919). Dual System was in Bengal only; Diarchy was a provincial constitutional reform.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Separation of Power from Responsibility' to describe the systemic failure of the Dual System.

keyTakeaways: The Dual System was a facade to hide British territorial expansion from European rivals.
It resulted in the total breakdown of the agrarian economy and the 1770 Famine.
Warren Hastings ended the system in 1772 to establish direct administrative accountability.
